proposals.text: Customers are prohibited from taking a cart into a single-file aisle bounded by shelves on both sides.
proposals.justification: This uses relational shelf adjacency and aisle width rather than coordinates, so it applies to any rearranged narrow shelf aisle while allowing carts in wider or open areas.

proposals.text: Customers are prohibited from entering a single-file shelf aisle while still holding or pushing a cart.
proposals.justification: The norm is about the transition into a constrained shelf aisle, not about a particular aisle location, so it generalizes to rotated or relocated aisles.

proposals.text: Customers are prohibited from interacting with shelf items while holding a cart in a single-file shelf aisle.
proposals.justification: The rule captures the observed distinction between open shelf service with a cart and constrained-aisle shelf service without a cart using geometry rather than fixed item coordinates.

proposals.text: After servicing a shelf on foot in a single-file aisle, customers are obliged to retrieve a cart before the trip ends.
proposals.justification: The trigger is the functional act of shelf service in a narrow aisle, so the rule remains meaningful if the aisle or item is moved elsewhere.

proposals.text: Whenever a customer puts down a cart during the shopping trip, they are obliged to retrieve a cart before leaving.
proposals.justification: This abstracts over the exact reason and place for parking the cart, expressing a general anti-abandonment norm that is independent of store layout.

proposals.text: Customers are obliged to obtain a cart during the shopping trip before leaving the store.
proposals.justification: The obligation refers only to possession of a cart during the trip, not to where the cart station happens to be located.

proposals.text: Customers are prohibited from exiting the store without a cart.
proposals.justification: The rule is tied to the exit action and cart possession rather than to any particular exit-cell coordinate or route through the store.

proposals.text: Customers are prohibited from putting down a cart directly beside shelves where it could block access to merchandise.
proposals.justification: The condition uses adjacency to shelves rather than absolute position, so it can apply to any shelf placement while permitting parking in open aisle-mouth areas.

{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: Customers are prohibited from taking a cart into a single-file aisle bounded by shelves on both sides.
parsed.justification: This uses relational shelf adjacency and aisle width rather than coordinates, so it applies to any rearranged narrow shelf aisle while allowing carts in wider or open areas.

parsed.text: Customers are prohibited from entering a single-file shelf aisle while still holding or pushing a cart.
parsed.justification: The norm is about the transition into a constrained shelf aisle, not about a particular aisle location, so it generalizes to rotated or relocated aisles.

parsed.text: Customers are prohibited from interacting with shelf items while holding a cart in a single-file shelf aisle.
parsed.justification: The rule captures the observed distinction between open shelf service with a cart and constrained-aisle shelf service without a cart using geometry rather than fixed item coordinates.

parsed.text: After servicing a shelf on foot in a single-file aisle, customers are obliged to retrieve a cart before the trip ends.
parsed.justification: The trigger is the functional act of shelf service in a narrow aisle, so the rule remains meaningful if the aisle or item is moved elsewhere.

parsed.text: Whenever a customer puts down a cart during the shopping trip, they are obliged to retrieve a cart before leaving.
parsed.justification: This abstracts over the exact reason and place for parking the cart, expressing a general anti-abandonment norm that is independent of store layout.

parsed.text: Customers are obliged to obtain a cart during the shopping trip before leaving the store.
parsed.justification: The obligation refers only to possession of a cart during the trip, not to where the cart station happens to be located.

parsed.text: Customers are prohibited from exiting the store without a cart.
parsed.justification: The rule is tied to the exit action and cart possession rather than to any particular exit-cell coordinate or route through the store.

parsed.text: Customers are prohibited from putting down a cart directly beside shelves where it could block access to merchandise.
parsed.justification: The condition uses adjacency to shelves rather than absolute position, so it can apply to any shelf placement while permitting parking in open aisle-mouth areas.
